sources.title: The Type of the Panama Canal
sources.supported_claim: The Board of Consulting Engineers' 8-5 vote split, the identities of the five minority (lock-canal) signers, Roosevelt's February 1906 message to Congress, and the June 1906 Senate vote of 36-31 approving the lock canal. Contemporary (1909) specialist science-journalism source, cross-checked against other sources below.

sources.title: Sea Level Canal (compiling Secretary of War William Howard Taft's 1906 report forwarding the majority and minority board reports to President Roosevelt)
sources.author_or_institution: Panama Canal history archive (Panama Canal Society / czbrats.com), quoting Taft's contemporary summary
sources.supported_claim: Secretary of War Taft's stated view that a sea-level canal would in principle be preferable but that its time and cost at Panama were 'in effect prohibitory' -- the direct rationale forwarded to Roosevelt ahead of his message to Congress.

sources.title: Panama Canal Construction, 1903-1914
sources.supported_claim: General chronology of the ICC's board process, the 8-5 majority/minority split, and the adoption of the minority (lock canal) report by the Isthmian Canal Commission.

sources.title: John Frank Stevens (biographical entry, American engineer & railroad builder)
sources.supported_claim: Stevens' appointment as chief engineer in 1905, his assessment that excavating Culebra to sea-level depth was impractical given slow prior progress and unstable geology, his lobbying for the lock-canal redesign, and his resignation in February 1907.

sources.title: The Panama Canal: Chief Engineers of the Panama Canal
sources.date: Documentary companion resource, publication date not specified on page
sources.supported_claim: Stevens' reasoning that the sea-level approach was made impractical by the unstable rock and mud of the Culebra cut, and his successful push for Isthmian Canal Commission approval of the lock-and-lake redesign.

sources.title: Panama Canal (event overview, resolution and legacy)
sources.supported_claim: General chronology cross-check: the 1914 opening of the canal, the earlier French effort's failure under Ferdinand de Lesseps, and the canal's role in global shipping through the 20th century.

sources.title: Panama Canal Expansion news release: Panama Canal Welcomes Largest Vessel To-Date Through New Locks
sources.author_or_institution: Autoridad del Canal de Panama (Panama Canal Authority)
sources.supported_claim: The scale of the 2016 Third Set of Locks expansion (new lock chambers roughly 427m x 55m x 18.3m vs. the original 1914 chambers of roughly 305m x 33.5m) and its purpose of accommodating Neopanamax vessels the original locks could not handle -- the basis for the unknown_at_t0 long-term nuance.

sources.title: Panama Canal Expansion - Third Locks
sources.supported_claim: Cross-check on the approximately $5.2 billion cost and 2016 completion date of the Third Set of Locks expansion project, and the reason it was undertaken (original locks too small for modern container ships).
